narrative.northStar: The Desktop Configuration Panel, Native on Phone
narrative.overview:
TailSplit retains the user-pinned desktop identity: neutral grouped surfaces, blue actions, text-backed semantic states, a plain green node check, and a fixed deep-gray diagnostic terminal. This mobile boundary keeps multiple Tailnets signed in with independent embedded device identities and one globally selected exit node. Native phone controls carry that identity; the desktop web typography and geometry are not transplanted into touch controls.

The implementation uses native UIKit Liquid Glass through `adaptive_platform_ui` for supported iOS controls on iOS 26+, with Cupertino fallback. The page content, inset grouped lists and node sheet include Flutter Cupertino widgets. Material 3 implementations also exist in source; Android has not been built or tested. This record describes the phone adaptation, not a new identity for TailSplit or a desktop redesign.
keyCharacteristics: System appearance and native semantic surfaces.
Native tab, toolbar, switch, segmented and menu controls where implemented.
System text for controls and content, Montserrat for large page titles.
Explicit connection state and staged node selection.
A diagnostic terminal with a constant dark palette.

rules.name: The Native Appearance Rule
rules.body: Resolve semantic platform surfaces and labels in context; reserve TailSplit's explicit colors for actions, state and the terminal.

rules.name: The State Rule
rules.body: Keep reachability, saved node choice and VPN connection distinct. A green reachable-node icon is not evidence that the VPN is connected.

rules.name: The Native Text Rule
rules.body: Use the system face for controls, sheet navigation and content; reserve Montserrat for large page titles. An inline toolbar title is native text. Preserve scaling supplied by the text widgets without claiming tested large-text layouts.

rules.name: The Native Material Rule
rules.body: Keep translucency in navigation and the reconnect bar; use native grouped surfaces for ordinary content.

dos: Do preserve the desktop's blue, semantic state and diagnostic-terminal identity through native roles.
Do use native semantic surfaces and system content text in both appearances.
Do distinguish connection state, reachability and a staged node choice with readable labels.
Do give every card-list row a platform icon, keep rows single-line and put supporting text below the group. Keep the green selected-node check and explicit confirmation.
Do preserve English/Chinese labels and source text scaling without claiming unverified accessibility conformance.
Do hide underlying native page toolbars while the picker sheet owns navigation, and disable tickers in inactive tabs.
donts: Don't treat Tailnet sign-ins as simultaneous VPN exits: list the accounts, but keep one global exit selection and one tunnel.
Don't add persistent selected-node row fill, fabricated latency, or a Ping action unsupported by the mobile data plane.
Don't equate simulated connected logs with verified account authorization or real VPN traffic.
Don't infer Android, tablet, large-text or older-iOS runtime verification from source branches.
